title: Correct, or be kind
hook: if you can, correct them; if not, kindness was given you for this (Meditations 9.11)

segments.voice: Yesterday: three presents. Your line was it suffices. When the wanting started, did enough hold? Day six hundred ten.

A friend says something you're fairly sure is wrong. Not dangerous, just wrong: a bad plan, a mistaken idea about a coworker, a choice about their kids. You can feel the correction loading in your mouth. And then a second voice: is this the moment? Will they hear it? Marcus met that fork too. In book nine he wrote down what to do when correcting doesn't work. Today: correct, or be kind.
screen: `THE CORRECTION LOADING.` → `IS THIS THE MOMENT?` → `CORRECT, OR BE KIND.`

segments.voice: First, the first branch. If you can, Marcus writes, set them right by teaching. Correction isn't forbidden. A friend who never tells you the truth isn't much of a friend. Second, the second branch. But if you can't, remember that kindness was given to you for exactly this. Not as decoration, not as a personality trait, but as equipment for this moment, the moment correction fails. Third, the surprising part. Even the gods, Marcus says, are kind to such people. They help them to health, to wealth, to reputation; that's how generous they are. Whatever you believe about the gods, look at the logic. If the highest powers keep helping people who get things wrong, then kindness can't be a prize for being right. It's given to the wrong as well. Fourth, the last line. And it's in your power too, he says. Or tell me: who's stopping you? His point: no circumstance can take away the ability to be kind. The other person can refuse your correction. Your kindness is yours to give whether they take it well or not. It's a close cousin of the third door, from book eight. Here the second door gets a warmer name. Not bear: be kind.
screen: `IF YOU CAN, CORRECT BY TEACHING.` · `IF NOT, KINDNESS WAS GIVEN FOR THIS.` · `EVEN THE GODS ARE KIND TO THEM.` · `WHO'S STOPPING YOU?` · then, large: `CORRECT OR BE KIND.`

segments.voice: Settle, and breathe. Think of one person you've wanted to correct lately. Picture the correction honestly. Could they hear it? Is it yours to give? If yes, picture saying it once, plainly and warmly, and then letting it go. If no, set it down. Let the point stay unmade for now, without keeping score. Instead, choose one kindness for that person, something small and concrete you could do this week. Hold your choice for a few breaths: correction, or kindness. The bell holds the time.
Correct. Marcus's two branches: if you can, correct by teaching; if you can't, remember that kindness was given you for this. Today's word.
Your line: who's stopping you. Choose one, on purpose, with one person today, and notice which one the moment really needed. Day six hundred ten.

howItsDone: People who draw on this entry often decide deliberately whether a correction can actually be heard; when it can't, they choose a concrete kindness instead of repeating the point.

fork.setup: your brother is set on a plan you think is a mistake. you've said so plainly, and he isn't listening. you're Marcus. what now?
options: remember kindness was given you for this, and be kind.
fork.reveal: if you can't correct them, Marcus writes, remember that kindness was given you for exactly this; even the gods are kind to such people.

original.note: Greek: kindness, goodwill. Marcus says it was given to us for this.

trapdoor: what you thought: be nice instead of honest.
what it means: correct when you can; when you can't, kindness is the tool made for that moment, and no one can stop you using it.
what a scholar hears: the argument runs from the gods: if divine powers help even those who err, human kindness can't depend on the other person being right.

notes: 9.11 paraphrased (Long: 'If thou art able, correct by teaching those who do wrong; but if thou canst not, remember that indulgence [benevolence] is given to thee for this purpose. And the gods, too, are benevolent to such persons; and for some purposes they even help them to get health, wealth, reputation; so good they are. And it is in thy power also; or say, who hinders thee?'). Confirm, including whether the Greek is εὐμένεια.
The outline's word is 'Correct' (title head); kept exactly.
